revisions.title: Readiness, or escape?
revisions.body: I hear this stretch as refusing an easy answer. If readiness for death is supposed to mark philosophical seriousness, what keeps that readiness from becoming mere impatience with life? Hold that distinction in mind: it is the pressure point I think gives the exchange its shape, before we decide whether Socrates has resolved it.

revisions.title: Release as discipline
revisions.body: The passage can be heard as placing two possibilities side by side: a life repeatedly governed by bodily satisfactions, and a life trained to loosen that grip. On this reading, hope is not an automatic escape promised by death; it is the name we give to a discipline already being attempted. The question is whether that discipline changes what release could mean.

revisions.title: When a contrary arrives
revisions.body: I hear this stretch as a change in level. The question is no longer how one thing can be described with opposite qualities, but what happens when the contrary approaches the principle or pattern that gives it that description. On this reading, snow, fire, and three make the issue concrete: they do not become their opposites while remaining what they are; they withdraw or perish. The passage thus sharpens a rule for testing identity.
